assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cells from a few percent (Miyasaka's 2009 dye-sensitized-type perovskite cells) to over 25 percent certified efficiency in about a decade, driven by a clear physical picture: large absorption, long carrier diffusion lengths, defect tolerance and tunable bandgaps. A new class of semiconductor processed from solution, with spin-off LEDs, detectors and tandems, is exactly the 'previously unforeseen opportunities' type of result I value; it sits at the physics-chemistry border and approaches a quantifiable limit (Shockley-Queisser).
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell; Park (solid-state 2012, ~9 percent) and Snaith (meso-superstructured/planar cells, ~10 percent and later vapour-deposited) turned it into a solid-state thin-film device. Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis made major contributions, so a three-person cut is contested. I would credit the founding cell plus the two groups that established the solid-state architecture.
assessment.maturity: Independent reproduction is overwhelming and efficiency records are replicated worldwide, but long-term stability, lead content and commercial deployment are unproven, so some members may argue recognition is early. Timing is defensible given the field's scale.
uncertainties: Stability and toxicity may still limit practical impact; committee may prefer to wait for commercial deployment.
Fair three-way split among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is unresolved; Gratzel's dye-cell background complicates priority.
Whether the citation should be framed as chemistry (materials synthesis) rather than physics (devices) is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of cells (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules, multivalent-interaction condensates) recasts intracellular organization in terms of soft-matter physics: phase diagrams, valency, critical concentrations. It is conceptually new, quantitatively formulated, and has generated a vast field across cell biology, neurodegeneration and biophysical chemistry. The physical principle is clear and of broad generality.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated liquid-like P granules in 2009; Rosen and Li et al. 2012 showed multivalent proteins drive phase separation in vitro with quantitative phase behavior. Pappu and Mittag contributed key theory and sequence-to-behavior principles. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen look like the most defensible core, though the allocation to Rosen versus Pappu or Mittag is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely, but debate continues on physiological relevance, concentrations used in vitro and whether some condensates are truly liquid phases; the interpretation is still evolving, which argues for caution on timing. Medicine or physiology may be the more natural home.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance of many reported condensates is contested.
Risk that the prize is judged more suited to biology than chemistry.
Credit for the in-vitro multivalency work versus the in-cell discovery needs resolution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion by orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs lets cells incorporate designed non-natural amino acids in proteins, giving chemists site-specific control of protein chemistry in vivo (photocrosslinkers, fluorophores, PTMs, bio-orthogonal handles). It is original, generalizable, and creates unforeseen capabilities for protein engineering and biophysics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues established the in vitro and then in vivo suppression approach and the first orthogonal pairs; Wang and Schultz extended to E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended to mammalian cells, multicellular organisms, and orthogonal ribosomes/quadruplet codons. Yokoyama and Mehl also contributed. Schultz, Chin and Wang are a coherent trio, but Chin's later contributions and Schultz's originality must be separated.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty years of independent use and widespread adoption in labs and biotech. The field is well established and timely.
uncertainties: Pyrrolysyl-tRNA synthetase work (Krzycki, Yokoyama, Chin) complicates attribution beyond the supplied names.
Overlap with earlier chemical aminoacylation work by Schultz and others on suppressor tRNAs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes drug action: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate proteins rather than inhibit them, opening the 'undruggable' proteome. The principle is clear and generative, and clinical candidates are in late stages.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept (2001); Crews's later work and Ciulli's VHL ligands and structure-guided degrader design made it practical. Handa, Ito and Sakamoto relate to thalidomide/cereblon molecular glue mechanism and are separate contributions; combining PROTACs and glues in one citation is a compound-discovery problem.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials but approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending; mechanistic confirmation of molecular glues (cereblon) is strong. Likely premature for a few more years, but timing is not unreasonable.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet, so impact remains prospective.
Compound discovery may require separating PROTACs from molecular glues, complicating the three-person limit.
Medicine-oriented overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the funnel concept provides a physical, quantitative account of how a protein can fold quickly without exhaustive search (Levinthal paradox), linking statistical mechanics, spin-glass physics and experiment. Its conceptual clarity and effect on protein structure prediction, folding kinetics and design are substantial; this is the kind of underlying principle I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes formulated the spin-glass/funnel idea; Onuchic extended it with structure-based models; Dill's hydrophobic-collapse and lattice models were an independent major framework; Fersht provided key experimental phi-value analysis. Wolynes, Onuchic and Dill is plausible, though Fersht's experimental role raises a theory-versus-experiment balance issue and Bryngelson's death or role is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental and computational support, with recent AI-based structure prediction (already recognized in 2024) overlapping the field. Interpretation is stable but the 2024 prize may reduce appetite for another protein-folding recognition.
uncertainties: The 2024 chemistry prize on structure prediction may make the committee reluctant to revisit protein folding.
Credit between Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Fersht is not cleanly resolved.
I am uncertain of the current status of some credited individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing, reading single polymer molecules through a pore via ionic current, is a physics-rich measurement principle that matured into a commercial sequencing technology with long reads, direct RNA and modification detection, and portable devices. Original concept, quantitative demonstration, and wide capability are all present.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer first showed single-stranded DNA translocation through alpha-hemolysin (1996); Bayley engineered pores for stochastic sensing and sequencing; Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled ratcheting and base discrimination leading to practical sequencing. Branton's current status (I believe he died in recent years but cannot verify) would restrict eligibility. Bayley, Deamer and Akeson is one candidate trio.
assessment.maturity: Commercial adoption and independent validation are strong; nanopore sequencing is widely used (genomes, pandemic surveillance). Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Eligibility of some credited founders is uncertain.
Medicine/physiology or physics might claim sequencing impact, but the measurement principle and pore engineering fit chemistry.
Allocation among Kasianowicz, Deamer, Branton, Bayley and Akeson is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Noncontact AFM with CO-functionalized tips resolves the bond-level structure of individual molecules, including bond order, intermediate products of on-surface reactions and molecular conformations. It is visually and quantitatively compelling, bringing physics instrumentation to bear directly on chemical structure, and has opened on-surface synthesis and single-molecule analysis.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl's qPlus sensor and frequency-modulation AFM made atomic resolution possible; Gross, Meyer and colleagues (IBM Zurich) introduced the CO-tip imaging of molecular structure in 2009; Eigler and Ho contributed to single-molecule manipulation and STM, which is a different earlier line (Binnig/Rohrer 1986 recognition). Gross, Meyer and Giessibl is a coherent trio.
assessment.maturity: Independently replicated in many labs; applications mostly in surface science and on-surface synthesis rather than routine chemical analysis, so broad chemical impact is more limited.
uncertainties: Impact on mainstream chemistry is narrower than other candidates.
Overlap with earlier physics prize for scanning probe microscopy may weigh against it.
Role of Pavlicek and others in the original work is not covered by supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis, based on reversible-terminator chemistry on clustered surfaces, reduced sequencing cost by orders of magnitude and transformed biology and medicine. The chemistry (reversible terminators, fluorescent nucleotides, solid-phase amplification) is the decisive step, and the lasting impact is enormous.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule array concept; Mayer and Farinelli's clustering at Manteia was an independent contribution; Rothberg's pyrosequencing-based 454 and Ju's work on terminators are parallel routes. Attribution among several parallel routes is genuinely hard.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and widely deployed, but the prize landscape (1980 sequencing prize, 2020s genomics) and the possibility that physiology or medicine would take it make the home category unclear.
uncertainties: Choice among competing platform lineages (Solexa, 454, Mayer/Manteia, Ju) is contested.
Possible overlap with earlier sequencing recognition.
Chemistry versus medicine fit.
